B.lives: A courtyard, a garden lit by hand-made lanterns: grown and cozy.

C.lives: absent; glass is slick and cold, though a choir is a voice.

D.lives: Herbarium: pressed herbs and garden almanacs, kept by night, the herbal touchstone.

E.lives: Warm light on a painting; no herb, moss or grown thing.

F.lives: Garden walls, moss grown quietly over them; only faintly herbal.

G.lives: A fairy ring of dancers: folk, grown in a circle like mushrooms.

I.lives: Pressed flowers and slow hours: a herbal pressing, grown and kept by hand.

J.lives: A lamp left burning in the garden: warm, tended, cozy as a kitchen.

K.lives: absent; its hush is the cold stillness I guard against.

L.lives: Slant light across a garden bed: the telling is slant, the herbs implied.

M.lives: Lamplight and night, cozy at a kitchen table; the music is not herbal.

N.lives: A hearth is cozy and home-made; glass is the slick, cold part I guard against.

O.lives: absent; stone and glass are the cold, sterile materials I guard against.
O.veto: The name is made only of slick, cold, sterile materials, the very things this guardian guards against.

note: A Herbarium of Nights is best because it names the herbal touchstone itself and keeps Medea's night-worked craft of pressed herbs.
